name: Wholana
tagline: TikTok research tool that ranks videos against each creator's own baseline and labels what they did

pricing.notes: Personal 5 USD/month, Plus 20 USD/month (adds the MCP server), Team 20 USD per seat with a 2-seat floor. Every plan starts with a free month.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.limits: 1 creator account for TikTok research and performance labeling

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 1 creator account plus ChatGPT and Claude analysis features

tiers.name: Team
tiers.notes: Minimum charge is $40/month because Team requires at least 2 seats.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly only, no annual plan published; card-backed first month free
pricing.hiddenCosts: Team has a 2-seat minimum ($40/month). The free month converts to paid unless cancelled; no annual discount or overage schedule is published.

verdictSummary: The core idea is simple arithmetic: a video's views divided by that creator's own median. An agent can build that for a watchlist of creators you pick, over a weekend, on top of a paid scraper API. What it cannot hand you is the corpus, hundreds of thousands of videos already scraped, deduped, and labeled against a curated craft taxonomy, which is what makes search across creators useful instead of a list of your own bookmarks. So: yes for watching 25 creators you already know, no for finding the ones you don't.
coreLoopDIY: Scrape a watchlist of creators nightly, compute each creator's rolling median views, and surface the videos that beat their own baseline.
requirements: TikTok scraper API (Apify or similar, paid per run)
LLM API key for hook labeling
a scrape budget that recurs every month
whatYouLose: search across videos you never chose to watch
a curated craft taxonomy instead of labels you invented
someone else absorbing the scrape cost and keeping it running
whyPeopleStillPay: The arithmetic is free, the data is not. A personal build only ever knows about the creators you thought to add, and you pay the scraper bill every month to keep even that fresh. The subscription is renting a corpus that was already collected and labeled, plus the discovery that only exists once videos from creators you have never heard of are sitting in the same index.

priorArt.name: TikTokApi
priorArt.desc: Unofficial Python wrapper for TikTok's web endpoints; gets you raw metrics, not a corpus, and breaks when TikTok changes

notes: Submitted by the maker, scored against the site's framework rather than the marketing page.
prompt:
Build me a personal TikTok outlier tracker to replace Wholana. Requirements:

- A nightly Node script (node-cron) that pulls recent videos for up to 25 handles listed in
  handles.txt, using a TikTok scraper actor on Apify, token in .env. Do not scrape TikTok
  directly, you will be blocked inside a day.
- Store videos in SQLite via better-sqlite3: handle, video id, url, caption, posted date,
  views, likes, comments, shares, date first seen. Upsert on video id so a re-scrape
  updates metrics instead of duplicating rows.
- Per creator, keep a rolling median of views over their last 30 videos and score each
  video as views divided by that median. 3x or higher is a breakout. Skip creators under
  10 videos, the median is noise below that.
- Label each breakout with one LLM call (Anthropic or OpenAI, key in .env): caption plus
  the first 15 seconds of subtitles from yt-dlp, returning one hook type from a fixed list
  of 12 in hooks.json. Fixed list, not free text, or nothing groups.
- A page on localhost:3000 (Express, server-rendered HTML, Chart.js): last 7 days of
  breakouts sorted by score, filterable by handle, each row showing score, views, hook
  type, and a link, plus a per-creator sparkline of views over time.
- A save button per row that writes the video into a swipe collection and appends it to
  swipe.md, so my picks survive the database.
- Localhost only. No accounts, no telemetry, everything on my machine except the Apify and
  LLM calls.
- Out of scope: search across creators I am not already tracking, and a shared craft
  taxonomy. Do not build auth, multi-user workspaces, or hosting config.
- README: Apify token and actor id, the cron entry, and the cost per 1,000 videos scraped.
  The scraper bill, not the code, is what makes people quit this build.
